successCriteria.description: src/shared/types/leave.types.ts exports four TypeScript enums — LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, LeaveBalanceStatus, EmployeeStatus — with exactly the reconciled-architecture values: LeaveType = ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY; LeaveRequestStatus = DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED (6 members); LeaveBalanceStatus = ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN; EmployeeStatus = ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION. No enum contains EXPIRED, PENDING, MATERNITY, PATERNITY, UNPAID, or OTHER (the stale root-ARCHITECTURE.md values).

src/shared/base-repository.ts exports a generic interface IBaseRepository<T> declaring exactly five methods — findById, findAll, create, update, delete — each with a Promise-returning signature appropriate to its semantics (single-entity lookup returns T | null, collection lookup returns T[], create/update return T, delete returns void or boolean). The interface is generic over T so that downstream phases can write ILeaveRepository extends IBaseRepository<LeaveRequest> without renaming methods.

The IBaseRepository<T> interface references the pg Pool type (imported from 'pg' or re-exported via src/shared/db/connection.ts) so that concrete repository implementations in later phases can inject the shared database pool. The interface compiles under strict TypeScript (strict:true, ES2022, commonjs, baseUrl ./src) with no implicit-any or type errors.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/shared/ as .test.ts files (matching jest.config.js testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)') and pass via ts-jest. The tests assert each enum's exact member set and string values, and verify that IBaseRepository<T> is structurally sound — i.e., a minimal object implementing all five methods satisfies the interface type at compile time (structural typing check) and the enum values match the reconciled architecture.

The full project type-checks and tests pass: `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0 and `npx jest` runs the new tests with zero failures. No new TypeScript compilation errors are introduced in src/ or tests/.

constraints: Enum values must follow the reconciled architecture (.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json + docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), NOT the stale root-level ARCHITECTURE.md. Specifically: LeaveRequestStatus must include UNDER_REVIEW (required by BR-007 sick-leave documentation workflow) and must NOT include PENDING; LeaveBalanceStatus must use FROZEN and must NOT include EXPIRED; LeaveType must be exactly ANNUAL/SICK/EMERGENCY (no MATERNITY/PATERNITY/UNPAID/OTHER).

TypeScript strict mode (strict:true, target ES2022, module commonjs, baseUrl ./src, rootDir ./src) must be satisfied with no implicit-any, no strict-null-check violations, and no unused declarations. The no-any HARNESS constraint (severity high) requires using unknown with type guards instead of any in any generic or helper code.

The IBaseRepository<T> method names — findById, findAll, create, update, delete — are fixed contracts: PLAN.md Phases 2–4 declare ILeaveRepository extends IBaseRepository<LeaveRequest>, IEmployeeRepository extends IBaseRepository<Employee>, and ILeaveBalanceRepository extends IBaseRepository<LeaveBalance>. Renaming any method or the generic parameter T would break downstream phases.

Follow the established module convention visible in src/modules/status/ and src/modules/uptime/: plain `export interface` for models in *.model.ts, `export interface I{Name}...` for service interfaces in *.interface.ts, and barrel index.ts re-exports. The new src/shared/types/ directory and src/shared/base-repository.ts must use the same export style (named exports, no default exports) for consistency.

This phase must not add @gestalt/* packages as dependencies (HARNESS no-gestalt-internal-deps, severity critical) and must not hardcode secrets (no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical). The only external dependency reference allowed is the existing pg package (already in package.json) for the Pool type.
outOfScope: Concrete repository implementations (e.g., KnexLeaveRepository, KnexEmployeeRepository, KnexLeaveBalanceRepository) — these are Phase 2–4. This phase only defines the IBaseRepository<T> interface contract, not any class that implements it or performs actual database queries.

Domain model interfaces (LeaveRequest, Employee, LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy) and their DTOs — these belong to Phase 2–4 module model files. This phase only defines the four shared enums and the base repository interface.

LeavePolicyStatus enum (ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, DEPRECATED) and any NotificationType / AuditAction / EntityType enums — these are not part of the four enums specified for this phase (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, LeaveBalanceStatus, EmployeeStatus). They may be introduced in later phases or modules.

Status transition rules, business-rule validation logic (BR-001 through BR-008), balance computation, and audit-log recording — these are service-layer concerns in Phases 5–8. The enums in this phase are pure value definitions with no transition or validation logic attached.

Database migrations, Knex configuration (knexfile), and table schema definitions — these are Phase 9. This phase references the pg Pool type only for the interface signature, not for schema or migration work.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum is a closed, static enumeration of exactly three leave categories (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY) with no lifecycle transitions. It is treated as a domain enum even though the reconciled architecture notes it may be stored as a reference table for extensibility; the enum values are the canonical codes.

The enum captures the full LeaveRequest lifecycle with six states: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. APPROVED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are terminal states. UNDER_REVIEW is a required intermediate state (per BR-007) reachable from SUBMITTED when sick-leave documentation is pending; CANCELLED is reachable from SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, or APPROVED. The enum must not include PENDING (a stale value) — SUBMITTED is the non-terminal active-review entry point.

The enum has exactly three states: ACTIVE (balance has remaining days available), EXHAUSTED (remaining is zero or below threshold), and FROZEN (balance locked, e.g., year-end or policy change). The enum must not include EXPIRED — FROZEN is the canonical locked state per the reconciled architecture.

The enum has exactly four employment states: ACTIVE (eligible for leave per BR-001), ON_LEAVE (currently on approved leave), INACTIVE (no longer active employee), and PROBATION (restricted eligibility — only leave types with probationEligible=true per BR-008). These states gate leave eligibility in downstream service logic.

The interface is a generic contract parameterized by entity type T, declaring exactly five data-access operations (findById, findAll, create, update, delete). It is the foundational abstraction that enforces GP-001 (all database access through repository interfaces) — no concrete database logic lives in this interface. It must be structurally extensible so that module-specific repository interfaces (ILeaveRepository, IEmployeeRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository) can extend it with their entity type without renaming or redefining the five base methods.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBaseRepository<T>.findById — retrieve a single entity by its unique identifier
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the entity of type T when found, or null/undefined when no record matches the identifier. Must not throw for a missing record (absence is a normal result, not an error). Errors from the underlying data source (connection failure, query error) propagate as rejected Promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBaseRepository<T>.findAll — retrieve a collection of entities
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array of T (empty array when no records exist, never null). Data-source errors propagate as rejected Promises. The operation is a pure read with no side effects.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBaseRepository<T>.create — persist a new entity and return the persisted record
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Accepts the data needed to create a new T, persists it, and returns the created entity (including any server-generated fields like id and timestamps). Constraint violations (duplicate key, FK failure) and data-source errors propagate as rejected Promises. This is a state-changing operation — downstream implementations must pair it with an audit record per GP-002.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBaseRepository<T>.update — modify an existing entity and return the updated record
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Accepts an identifier and the partial or full update data, applies the change, and returns the updated T. If the target record does not exist, the result is null/undefined or a rejected Promise (the interface contract must document which, but absence is not a silent success). Data-source errors propagate as rejected Promises. This is a state-changing operation — downstream implementations must pair it with an audit record per GP-002.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IBaseRepository<T>.delete — remove an entity by its unique identifier
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Accepts an identifier and removes the corresponding record. Returns void or a boolean/affected-rows indicator. Deleting a non-existent record is not an error (idempotent removal). Data-source errors propagate as rejected Promises. This is a state-changing operation — downstream implementations must pair it with an audit record per GP-002.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The four enum member sets must exactly match the reconciled architecture artifact. LeaveType: ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY. LeaveRequestStatus: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. LeaveBalanceStatus: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN. EmployeeStatus: ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION. The reconciled.json domain_entities and architecture_md_update sections are the single source of truth; the stale root-level ARCHITECTURE.md (which lists MATERNITY/PATERNITY/UNPAID/OTHER and PENDING) must NOT be matched.

The enum values must be consistent with the "Lifecycle States" section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the gestalt-managed architecture block), which lists: LeaveRequest = DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED; Employee = ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION; LeaveBalance = ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN; LeaveType = (static, ANNUAL/SICK/EMERGENCY). This is the human-readable mirror of reconciled.json and must agree with it.

The IBaseRepository<T> interface (or its concrete implementations in later phases) must reference the same pg Pool type that src/shared/db/connection.ts exports via `new Pool(...)`. The connection module is the single source of the database pool; the base repository interface must be compatible with injecting this pool so that downstream KnexLeaveRepository/KnexEmployeeRepository/KnexLeaveBalanceRepository classes can use it without a second pool instantiation.

The export style of the new shared types and base repository must match the established barrel-export convention: named exports only (no default exports), with index.ts re-exporting public symbols. src/modules/status/index.ts demonstrates the pattern (`export { X } from './x'`). The new src/shared/types/leave.types.ts and src/shared/base-repository.ts must follow the same named-export style for cross-module consistency.

All new source files must compile under the existing tsconfig.json settings: strict:true, target ES2022, module commonjs, baseUrl ./src, rootDir ./src. Source files live under src/ (included); test files live under tests/ (excluded from tsc compilation but compiled by ts-jest at test time). The enum and interface code must not rely on compiler options absent from this config (e.g., no experimental decorators, no enum string-value assumptions beyond standard TS enum semantics).

Test files must match the jest.config.js testMatch pattern '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)' and be compiled by the ts-jest preset in the node test environment. Tests must be placed under tests/unit/shared/ with a .test.ts extension. The moduleDirectories ['node_modules', 'src'] setting means imports can resolve from src/ without relative path prefixes — test imports of the shared types and base repository must be consistent with this resolution.

integrationPoints.why: The IBaseRepository<T> interface must be type-compatible with the shared database pool exported from connection.ts. This is the only existing dependency for this phase — the interface references the Pool type so that concrete repository implementations in Phases 2–4 can inject the pool. No new database connection is created.

The IBaseRepository<T> interface and its five method names (findById, findAll, create, update, delete) are the contract that Phase 2's ILeaveRepository will extend. The generic parameter T and method signatures established here must remain stable so that the leave repository interface can extend it without modification.

integrationPoints.target: PLAN.md Phase 3 — src/modules/employee/employee.repository.ts (IEmployeeRepository extends IBaseRepository<Employee>) and Phase 4 — src/modules/balance/balance.repository.ts (ILeaveBalanceRepository extends IBaseRepository<LeaveBalance>)
integrationPoints.why: The EmployeeStatus enum (from leave.types.ts) is consumed by the Employee model in Phase 3, and the LeaveType + LeaveBalanceStatus enums are consumed by the LeaveBalance model in Phase 4. Both repository interfaces extend IBaseRepository<T>. The enum values and interface contract defined in this phase are the foundation for all downstream module repositories.

The IBaseRepository<T> interface is the structural enforcement point for the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint (severity critical) and GP-001. By defining the repository interface here, all downstream database access is channeled through it. The interface itself must use typed generics (T) rather than any to satisfy the no-any constraint (severity high).
